column1: *** AND THE RUN STARTED BY LOSING A VOLUME TO A FAULT THAT WOULD HAVE BEEN INVISIBLE ***
column2: the first attempt died on its opening volume with curl exit 56 — a dropped connection partway through 162 MB — AND THE SCANNER HAD NO RETRY. That turns a network blip into a volume silently missing from a sweep that then reports itself complete. It is the same class of error as a blind OCR layer: not a wrong answer, an UNEARNED one. Retry, resume and a stall timeout were added and the run restarted from the top. Charlottenburg 1968 then took 971 seconds against 60 for its neighbours — it was retrying the whole time, and it finished.

column2: page 80 of P Rep. 721 Nr. 2767. "Gesch." is GESCHIEDEN, so Leibholz is most likely her own name and Katznol the marriage she left. NOT YET CONFIRMED AT THE IMAGE and the death date is not yet read.

column1: *** GERDA FELICITAS BADE geb. LEIBHOLZ — WILMERSDORF 1993 NR. 312 ***
column2: died 15 February 1993, entered TWICE — "Bade geb. Leibholz" on page 7 and "Leibholz" on page 74, the same register number from two unrelated positions. A LEIBHOLZ-BORN WOMAN WHO MARRIED OUT, which is exactly the case row 253 insisted the L block be read for. NOT YET CONFIRMED AT THE IMAGE.

column1: *** MARGARETHE GERTRUD LEIPHOLZ gesch. DRIESEN — TEMPELHOF 1967 NR. 2201 ***
column2: died 5 NOVEMBER 1967, ev. Page 140 of P Rep. 150 Nr. 383, under the 1967 heading, between Lüdtke geb. Wolff and Lange geb. Behlendorf. CONFIRMED AT THE IMAGE. Found only because that volume HAS NO TEXT LAYER AT ALL and was read page by page instead.

column1: WHAT THAT TOTAL MEANS AGAINST WHAT CAME BEFORE
column2: BEFORE 7 OCTOBER THIS ARCHIVE HELD ONE LEIBHOLZ DEATH IN ANY BERLIN REGISTER — Günther, Schöneberg 1939 Nr. 780. It now holds six people across the two spellings from these two sweeps, plus Erna Frida Else Leipholz 1975, Fritz Leipholz 1985, Marie Leipholz 1988 and Gertrud Ella Meiritz geb. Leipholz 1993 from the day before.

column1: AND THREE OF THEM CARRY THE NAME IN THEIR OWN RIGHT
column2: HILDE has no "geb." at all; GERDA was born Leibholz and married Bade; HERTHA is "gesch." A woman BORN Leibholz had Leibholz parents in Berlin within living memory, and the marriage that made Gerda a Bade would name her father on a document. That is a different and better kind of lead than a death entry.

column1: and the pattern that was called a pattern rather than a rule, correctly
column2: Charlotte is geb. Schötzow and Ella is geb. Baesler — both married IN. On that evidence this file was about to say that birth registers are the wrong instrument for these women. HILDE, GERDA AND HERTHA BROKE IT WITHIN THE HOUR. Two for two became two for five.

column1: why they are probably somebody else
column2: the Neukölln sweep of 7 October produced LEOKADIA LOWINSKI née BARANIAK, katholisch — the POLISH CATHOLIC strand the family tree once confused with Derrick's line. The Steglitz 1983 entry is also RK. This archive's Luwinskis are Jewish on one side and the spelling LOWINSKI is an ordinary Polish-German surname living in Berlin attached to other families. RECORDED SO THEY ARE NOT REDISCOVERED AS RELATIVES.

column1: # ---------------- SIX VOLUMES WITH NO TEXT LAYER, AND WHAT WAS DONE ABOUT THEM ----------------
*** TEMPELHOF 1967-1968, P Rep. 150 Nr. 383 — READ AT THE IMAGE, AND IT MATTERED ***
column2: 288 pages, NOT ONE carrying text. The L block is pages 136 to 149, bounded by the end of K on 135 and the opening of M on 150; the 1967 run is 136-145 and the 1968 run 146-149, both headings read. ONE LEIPHOLZ (above) AND NO LEIBHOLZ. *** THAT IS THE CHECK THAT PROTECTS THE CHARLOTTE READING: *** she leaves the Neukölln directory in 1967 and her candidate dies in Tempelhof in 1982, so a second Charlotte Leibholz dying in Tempelhof in 1967 or 1968 would have undercut it. There is none.

column1: and this volume is the second to show the bracket is not a proof of coverage
column2: ITS L BLOCK IS NOT ALPHABETICAL. Page 136 opens L with Likerske, Lorke, Lehmann, Langer, Langer, Lüdtke, Lorey, Lange — the entries run BY DATE. Neukölln 1967-68 does the same. In a book ordered like that, nearest-name-either-side means nothing and only reading every page of the letter works.

column1: *** ALL SIX BLIND VOLUMES ARE NOW READ AT THE IMAGE. THE SWEEP IS 193 OF 193. ***
column2: None of the five remaining holds a Leibholz or a Leipholz, and each is bracketed or bounded in its own way rather than simply scanned.

column1: TIERGARTEN 1967, P Rep. 820 Nr. 30 — pages 84 to 92
column2: Bounded by the end of K on 83 and the opening of M on 93. NOT ALPHABETICAL INSIDE THE LETTER — it runs by month, with a December heading at the end — so every page was read. NOTHING. The run holds LEVY verh. Deuser and LILIENFELD verh. Krüger, recorded because they are on the leaf and not because they mean anything.

column1: TIERGARTEN 1968, P Rep. 820 Nr. 31 — pages 85 to 93
column2: Bounded by K on 84 and M on 94, January heading at the top and December at the foot, every page read. NOTHING. *** THESE TWO MATTER BECAUSE TIERGARTEN IS WHERE ELLA WAS FOUND: *** her entry is 1974, and had a second Leibholz been sitting in the same office in 1967 or 1968 the 1974 candidate would have been weaker. There is none.

column1: WILMERSDORF 1990, P Rep. 570 Nr. 3031 — settled on ONE page
column2: Typewritten and ALPHABETICAL, so the whole question lands on page 63: the sequence runs LEHMBECK then LEIBELT with nothing between, and LEIPACHER then LEIPOLD with nothing between. BOTH SLOTS BRACKETED TIGHT. L runs pages 61 to 66.

column1: CHARLOTTENBURG 1990, P Rep. 559 Nr. 1444 — pages 92 to 96
column2: Also typewritten and alphabetical. Page 94 closes LEHNHÄUSER geb. Volkmann · LEIBNER geb. Gillert · Leiche, and page 95 opens Leiche · LEIDER · LEIPZIGER. LEIBHOLZ WOULD SIT BETWEEN LEHNHÄUSER AND LEIBNER AND LEIPHOLZ BETWEEN LEIDER AND LEIPZIGER. Neither is there.

column1: TEMPELHOF 1914-1979, P Rep. 150 Nr. 752 — pages 147 to 162
column2: *** THE ODD ONE, AND THE LONGEST REACH IN THE WHOLE SWEEP. *** A single retrospective volume covering SIXTY-FIVE YEARS, written in KURRENT, arranged by letter and then by YEAR inside each letter — 1917, 1918, 1919 and so on, with a RELIGION column and a "Nr. des Registers". Bounded by K on 145 and M on 163, every page read. NOTHING. Nearest in the run: LEITHOLD and LEISTIKOW.

column1: what the six blind volumes cost and why they were worth it
column2: THEY ARE 1,270 PAGES THAT NO TEXT SEARCH CAN EVER TOUCH, in five different hands and four different arrangements. Had they been left out, the sweep would have been 97 per cent of West Berlin reported as 100 per cent — and one of them, Tempelhof 1967-68, turned out to hold a LEIPHOLZ nobody would ever have found by searching.

column1: STILL TO READ AT THE IMAGE, AND RECORDED AS UNREAD RATHER THAN COUNTED AS NEGATIVE
column2: CHARLOTTENBURG 1990 (Nr. 1444, 192 pp) · TEMPELHOF 1914-1979 (Nr. 752, 297 pp, a retrospective volume) · TIERGARTEN 1967 (Nr. 30, 183 pp) · TIERGARTEN 1968 (Nr. 31, 177 pp) · WILMERSDORF 1990 (Nr. 3031, 133 pp). column1: *** AGNES née KERGER, Mehringdamm 109 — STILL MISSING AND HER BOROUGH IS EXHAUSTED ***
column2: Kreuzberg 1980-1994 read 7 October, eleven volumes by a text layer that proves its own eyesight plus 1983 at the image, and she is in none of it. She left the telephone book after 1979-80 at the age of ninety-one. SHE IS THE ONE THIS SWEEP HAS NOT ANSWERED, and more volumes is not obviously the answer — a home in another borough, or a death registered where she was nursed, is at least as likely.
